# NL rejection tests fail on their deliberately provoked worker errors

## Context

The three intentional-error rows in #17844 were independently reproduced together on `dev@633585423d2d7e8a33fd131ed265e199f110b5e2`: `CreateInstance`, `DisconnectReleaseNL`, and `MultiWriterNL` all reached their semantic assertions, then failed the automatic worker-error gate. The run completed in 5s with 3 failed tests.

## The Problem

The tests deliberately exercise rejection, but never declare its worker-console counterpart. `CreateInstance` logs both `Class Neo.missing.DoesNotExist does not exist` and `Store not found: <the just-undone store>`. The write-guard tests log the intended overlapping-write conflict, including transient conflict responses while disconnect cleanup is pending. These are exactly the requests whose rejection the tests assert; unmatched errors must remain failures.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/ai/Client.mjs#onSocketMessage` logs an App Worker error before sending a JSON-RPC rejection. `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs#workerErrors` provides `expect(RegExp)` for specifically named errors and rejects every other captured worker/page error. The existing `core/WorkerErrorGate.spec.mjs` proves named errors pass and unnamed errors fail. The module-bearing create config is rejected in the service wrapper before reaching the App Worker and needs no worker-error declaration.

## The Fix

Use the existing `workerErrors` fixture in the three existing specs. Match the complete tested error category and exact runtime target, with literal IDs escaped in regexes. Retain and tighten semantic assertions so a wrong denial cause cannot become a pass. Keep sibling-write admission, post-disconnect eventual admission, create/undo behavior and the global error gate unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three complete specs pass with declarations limited to the exact missing class, undone store, and tested write-conflict target; all existing success/admission assertions remain.
- [ ] An unrelated worker error still fails a repaired spec (negative control), and removing an expected-error declaration restores its original gate failure.
- [ ] The existing worker-error gate controls remain green; no production or shared-fixture behavior changes.

## Out of Scope

WriteGuard policy, Client error logging, general error suppression, other battery failures, new test helpers or public APIs.

## Avoided Traps

Do not waive the whole `Neo.ai.Client` error category or accept any returned RPC error. A write denied for a different reason or target must still fail. Disconnect cleanup is asynchronous: preserve the existing bounded admission poll rather than assuming socket close has synchronously released the lock.
